issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse referral under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, when the suit’s subject matter and substantive reliefs extend beyond the arbitration agreement and involve non-signatories to it.

An arbitration clause in a licence agreement does not extend to separate tripartite mortgage and loan arrangements merely because they relate to the same property or arise from the parties’ broader contractual relationship.
A suit involving connected claims against parties to and non-parties to an arbitration agreement cannot be split so that only part of the dispute is referred to arbitration.
Consent by non-signatories to arbitration cannot create an arbitration agreement in a separate transaction that contains no arbitration clause.
